pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented and genuinely tailored — the rep tied the mobility-first approach directly to the disclosed back and joint problems: 'especially with your joints being stiff, your, you know, the back pain, one of the first thing we're going to do is design and give you a mobility routine.' The prospect was taking notes throughout and answered 'Nope. I'm just writing the notes down' when asked for questions, then 'Yeah' to whether it would help. He had already validated the modality unprompted before the pitch: 'I saw his mobility exercises and I was like, man, that was good. And so I started doing those five minute deals in the morning. That's exactly what I needed to be doing.'

Presented as the primal eating protocol with no macro tracking. Response was a single 'Yep.' He had already established that he eats whole foods, avoids fast food and additives, and stays within 1,800-2,200 calories, and his wife's coeliac disease means they do not eat out — so this pillar carried almost no weight for him and neither party pretended otherwise.

Presented as the app, daily workouts, 24/7 access to Trevor, at-least-weekly check-ins and form-video review. Response: 'Cool' and then 'No, it's super self-[explanatory], really' when asked for questions. Worth noting he later contradicted the value of one part of it in passing: told about a coach who said 'no excuses, do it anyway', he replied 'if that guy was like, do it anyway, I mean, that wouldn't be helpful for me... Sometimes you need to be encouraged strongly' — the only nuance he offered about how he wants to be held to account.

anchors.raw: I saw his mobility exercises and I was like, man, that was good. And so I started doing those five minute deals in the morning. That's exactly what I needed to be doing.
anchors.note: The second call in this batch where the prospect is already extracting the value he came for from the founder's free content. He found Trevor on Facebook reels, was not following him before, and is already running the mobility routines that the pitch positions as phase one. A content-led funnel repeatedly produces prospects who have already banked the first deliverable for nothing.

anchors.raw: it just depends on what you're going to tell me, because I have no knowledge of where this is going. You know, if you sit there and tell me this is $5,000 a month, no, I'm not ready to do that. I just need to know more information.
anchors.note: He arrived with no reference price whatsoever, having never bought coaching of any kind: 'I've just never had to make a decision like this before.' With nothing to compare against, $6,000 landed as an absolute rather than a relative number, and he said so — 'Have I ever spent this much money on something like this? No.' The rep had a clear invitation to build the frame before quoting and did not.

anchors.raw: we're building a house right now. It's a lot of money too.
anchors.note: Reinforced later by 'having an emergency fund to consider'. His discretionary capital is already committed to a house under construction, which is why capacity ('of course I have the money') and willingness diverged so sharply. This is the same competing-spend shape that blocked the Tim Wigg call and the script has no play for it.

anchors.raw: It's just, I'm a tight wad. And, you know, $6,000 to work out is, that's a big investment.
anchors.note: Stated twice and volunteered as the actual blocker after value and capacity had both been ruled out. This is an identity anchor rather than a number, and it is the one the rep needed to work with: a man who defines himself by discipline and by not spending money, where the discipline identity was the available lever and was never used.

anchors.raw: if you're looking at just, dude, am I paying $6,000 to work out? Like, I could work out for free. Like, I don't think that's the most, that's not how I would look at it.
anchors.note: The rep put the cheapest alternative into words himself, on behalf of a prospect who had not raised it. The prospect had in fact already conceded value — 'your health is invaluable. So it's not about that' — so this articulated an objection that was not live.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that loaded kettlebell training is appropriate for unhealed slipped lumbar discs that have hurt at six to seven out of ten for twenty years, after doctors, x-rays and chiropractors.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed. The rep asserted the programme would be 'freeing up all the joint pain' and attributed joint pain generally to posture, but nothing was said about the discs specifically, no clearance was sought, and a load-progression target was set instead: 'wherever you start... we tangibly got you at least another eight kilos heavier.'

unmet_demand.want: To know what equipment to buy and at what weight before committing. He had read a recommendation in the pre-call notes and raised it directly.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The recommendation he had been given was contradicted on the call ('30 kilos might be way too heavy, you know, especially if you have back issues') and the actual answer was deferred to a strength test that only happens after purchase: 'we kind of do like a bit of a strength test when a new client signs up.' He left with no equipment spec and no equipment budget.

unmet_demand.want: Evidence that the company is legitimate before wiring $6,000 to a stranger — 'I don't know anything about your company... I've been screwed before.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No testimonials, client references, results, refund policy or third-party proof were offered. The only risk-reversal produced was an improvised $1,200 thirty-day arrangement invented on the spot, which he declined. For a prospect whose stated blocker included provider risk, there was nothing standard to hand him.

unmet_demand.want: Accountability that pushes hard rather than accommodating — 'Sometimes you need to be encouraged strongly.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep had just positioned the programme's flexibility as the differentiator, using a story about a coach who said 'no excuses, do it anyway' as the negative example. The prospect half agreed and half disagreed, and the distinction was never resolved. The programme may well deliver both; nobody established it.
